land.text: Roussillon, 'occupied by the Carolingians in 760' after Pepin the Short's defeat of the Saracens in 759

predecessors.note: The County page's infobox says 'Establishment: 759' and its text 'probably conquered for the Frankish Empire by Pepin the Short and his Visigothic allies in 760'. Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks row (462-849) is the overlord; West Francia (west-franks, from 850) after it.

land.text: the whole county: 'On the death of Gerard II without heirs in 1172, Roussillon passed' to Alfonso II of Aragon

successors.note: The Roussillon page: Girard II 'left all his lands to Alfonso II of Aragon, who took possession in 1172'. The Crown of Aragon dossier holds the 19 cells from 1172 (its 1177 shape). Cerdanya and Roussillon were held again as an appanage by Sancho I and Nuño Sánchez from about 1209 to 1242 (county-of-berga, crown-of-aragon); that is not this state.

capitals.name: Castellrosselló (Ruscino, by Perpignan)
capitals.note: The page says only that 'Giselbert moved the capital of Roussillon from Castellrosellón to a village named Perpignan', without a year; the move is placed at Giselbert I's accession in 989 (Empúries page: 'Giselbert I received Roussillon'). The earlier years (759-988) assume the same seat; no page names a capital before Giselbert. Coordinates are the researcher's.

capitals.name: Perpignan
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Perpignan'; chosen 'in preference to the episcopal seat of Elna'. Year of the move not on the page (see the previous entry).

correction.text: the county round Perpignan, Elna and the Conflent, Vallespir and Têt valleys as Cliopatria draws it in 896, without Empúries (which Gaucelm received only in 817)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 759-816: Cliopatria begins in 896 but the County page's infobox says 'Establishment: 759' (text: conquered 'in 760'; the Roussillon page: 'occupied by the Carolingians in 760'). No page gives an extent for these years; Roussillon alone (Cliopatria's 896 outline without the three Empúries cells, since Empúries was joined only in 817) stands in.

correction.text: Roussillon united with Empúries and Peralada (the 896 outline applied back to 817)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 817-895: 'The first count known by name, Gaucelm, received the County of Empúries in 817' and 'The counties of Roussillon and Empúries remained united until 989'. Cliopatria's 896 outline (20 cells, 4,652 km2) already holds the union, so it is applied back to 817; Cliopatria's own row starts in 896 (the Roussillon page dates the first hereditary count, Sunyer II, to 893).

896-989, 4,652 km2 (20 H3 cells: the Roussillon plain, Conflent, Vallespir, the Alt Empordà round Empúries and Roses). The infobox gives no area (the Roussillon page gives 3,600 km2 for the modern département, ratio about 0.8 to this outline without Empúries); the union with Empúries to 989 is on the page.

correction.text: Roussillon after the separation from Empúries in 989

keyframe_review.note: 990-999, 4,676 km2 (19 cells): Cliopatria keeps Empúries inside Roussillon until 999, but 'At the death of Gausfred I in 989, Roussillon and Empúries were separated' (Empúries page). The three Empúries cells come out; Cliopatria's Empúries row starts only in 1000. The page also says 'Late in the 10th century, Alt Rosselló, Conflent, and inland Vallespir passed to the counts of Cerdanya' (no year; the Wilfred the Hairy page, read for county-of-urgell, has Miró ruling 'over Cerdanya and Conflent' after 897): Cliopatria still draws those valleys as Roussillon to 1172 and they are not taken out here (see notes).

correction.text: the 1003 outline applied to 1000-1002: Roussillon without Empúries, with the Collioure-Banyuls coast

keyframe_review.note: 1000-1002, 3,796 km2 (16 cells): this outline lacks the three coastal cells (Collioure, Banyuls) that the 990 and 1003 outlines hold; no page records a loss and none a gain, so the 1003 outline (19 cells) is used for these years. Empúries is separate in all of them.

1003-1065, 4,128 km2 (19 cells). The Empúries invasion of 1014 and the pact of 1019 ('In 1014, Hugh I of Empúries invaded Roussillon, but in 1019 a pact was signed making the two counties permanently separate') move no border; the Roussillon page does not name ground held.
1066-1168, 4,056 km2: the same 19 cells as the 1003 outline (the geometry differs in vertices only); nothing on the pages explains a change in 1066.

correction.text: the 1169 shape unchanged, holding 1169-1171 only; from 1172 the land is the Crown of Aragon's

keyframe_review.note: 1169-1176, 4,056 km2: the same 19 cells. The county ended in 1172 ('Girard II left all his lands to Alfonso II of Aragon, who took possession in 1172'), so the shape holds for 1169-1171 only; 1172-1176 are the Crown of Aragon's (its 1177 shape holds these 19 cells).

region.text: Roussillon, the later county round Perpignan and Elna

ledger.note: 759: the Carolingian county of Roussillon is established. The County page's infobox says 'Establishment: 759'; its text says 'probably conquered for the Frankish Empire by Pepin the Short and his Visigothic allies in 760'; the Roussillon page: 'In 719, the Saracens crossed the Pyrenees and maintained political hegemony of Septimania until their final defeat in 759 ... Roussillon was occupied by the Carolingians in 760.' The page names the land, not an outline.

region.text: Empúries, with Peralada, a separate county 'around 813 ... under Ermenguer' and merged with Roussillon in 817

ledger.note: 817: Gaucelm receives Empúries and the two counties are joined. 'In 817, Empúries was merged with the County of Roussillon, a union which lasted until 989.' The Roussillon page: 'The first count known by name, Gaucelm, received the County of Empúries in 817.'

989: Gausfred I dies and Empúries is separated from Roussillon. 'At the death of Gausfred I in 989, Roussillon and Empúries were separated.' Gausfred's elder son Hugh I took Empúries and Giselbert I Roussillon (Empúries page, undated sentence). Cliopatria keeps the Empúries cells in Roussillon to 999.

About 989: Giselbert I moves the seat from Castellrosselló to Perpignan. The page says 'Giselbert moved the capital of Roussillon from Castellrosellón to a village named Perpignan' and gives no year; 989 is the researcher's bridge (Giselbert's accession), so the year is a gap.

region.text: the frontier between Empúries and Roussillon, 1014-1019; the page says only that Hugh I 'invaded Roussillon'

ledger.note: 1014: Hugh I of Empúries invades Roussillon. 'In 1014, Hugh I of Empúries invaded Roussillon, but in 1019 a pact was signed making the two counties permanently separate.' The page names no ground held, so the zone is the frontier band between the two Cliopatria shapes, matching the Empúries dossier.

region.text: the frontier between Empúries and Roussillon, 1014-1019

ledger.note: 1019: the pact. 'in 1019 a pact was signed making the two counties permanently separate.'

1172: Roussillon passes to Alfonso II of Aragon. 'To ensure that his brothers would not inherit his territories, in his will Girard II left all his lands to Alfonso II of Aragon, who took possession in 1172.' The County page (infobox 'Annexed into the Principality of Catalonia: 1172'): 'On the death of Gerard II without heirs in 1172, Roussillon passed, as per prior agreement of the nobles...' to Alfonso. The Crown of Aragon dossier carries the matching gain.

1172: the county of Roussillon ends as a separate state when Alfonso II takes it (infobox 'Annexed into the Principality of Catalonia: 1172'). Alfonso held an assembly at Perpignan in 1173 'where he declared a peace for all Roussillon and the diocese of Elna'.

wars.name: Empúries-Roussillon war (1014-1019)

zones.text: the frontier between Empúries and Roussillon; the page names no ground

wars.outcome: Hugh I of Empúries invaded Roussillon in 1014; a pact of 1019 made the two counties permanently separate. No border moved.
wars.note: The Empúries page does not mention the invasion or the pact (checked); only the Roussillon page does. The page names neither a battle nor the ground held.

certainty.note: A Pyrenean and coastal county whose pages name towns and valleys, not lines; the frontier with Empúries is the best known (separated in 989, pact of 1019) but is still a stand-in outline; the Conflent and Vallespir frontier with Cerdanya is disputed between pages.

notes:
Written by the Phase B agent eu-12-b on 2026-10-25 from three pages (budget 5). WebFetch returns a few paragraphs as paraphrase; quoted fragments are the tool's, kept short.
START AND END. The County page's infobox gives 759 and 1172; Cliopatria draws 896-1176. Keyframes were added for 759-816 and 817-895 (no page gives an extent; Cliopatria's 896 outline stands in, without Empúries before 817). The state ends in 1172 (Crown of Aragon dossier: gain of the 19 cells in 1172); Cliopatria's 1169 shape runs to 1176, so 1172-1176 belong to the Crown.
EMPÚRIES. Union 817-989 (Empúries page and Roussillon page agree); Cliopatria keeps the Empúries cells in the Rosselló row until 999 and starts its Empúries row in 1000: the 990 shape is adjusted and the 1000 shape replaced by the 1003 outline (it lacks the Collioure-Banyuls coast). The 1014 invasion and the 1019 pact are on the Roussillon page only.
UNSETTLED. (1) Conflent, Alt Rosselló and inland Vallespir: the Roussillon page says 'Late in the 10th century, Alt Rosselló, Conflent, and inland Vallespir passed to the counts of Cerdanya', the Wilfred the Hairy page (read for county-of-urgell) has Miró ruling 'over Cerdanya and Conflent' after 897, and county-of-berga records Vallespir going with Besalú in 988 and coming to Cerdanya in 1111. Cliopatria draws the valleys as Roussillon throughout, no page gives a year or an extent, and nothing is taken out here: the land may belong to county-of-berga, county-of-besalu or this state in 990-1172. (2) The capital move to Perpignan has no year (placed at 989, confidence 1). (3) No page gave an area for the county; the only figure is 3,600 km2 for the modern Pyrénées-Orientales. (4) Girard I's crusade (1099) and the 1173 Perpignan assembly are on the pages but move no border. (5) No ruler list: the pages give no reign years, so identity.rulers is omitted.
Gazetteer names needed: none; the regions used resolve ('Roussillon', Cliopatria shapes, border band).
